gate.model_gate: The user explicitly overrode the lesson-factory Fable-only gate for this report-only preflight.
gate.reason: The course entry, research brief, prerequisite chapters, concept registry, and notation ledger agree on one move: denser samples of a fixed finite-record DTFT improve localization of one modeled peak, while physical resolution changes only when the informative observation or window changes.

course_contract.goal: Estimate sinusoidal frequency and amplitude without confusing spectral interpolation with physical resolution.
course_contract.opening_verbatim: A sampled main lobe can locate one isolated tone between bins, but denser FFT samples do not add observation time or separate unresolved components.
inherits: Windows, Leakage, and Resolution established that a finite record has a window-shaped DTFT, and fixed coherent-gain, scalloping, main-lobe, sidelobe, and ENBW conventions.
FFT Factorization and Machine Layout established that an FFT changes the evaluation schedule, not the declared DFT coefficients, and that transform length, order, and scale are interface clauses.
must_not_reteach: The derivation of window convolution, the window-comparison table, coherent gain, scalloping, or ENBW.
FFT factorization, butterflies, bit reversal, operation counts, or library benchmarking.
The PaddingVsDataLab result already used by the DFT lesson; this chapter may retrieve its conclusion but must use a new fixed-data-versus-longer-data visual contract.
course_contract.hands_off: The closing exercise exposes the variability of one-bin squared magnitude; correlation-psd-and-welch owns random-process definitions, autocorrelation, PSD normalization, periodogram consistency, and Welch averaging.

single_conceptual_move.statement: Separate localization from resolution: zero padding and a local peak model refine the coordinate and amplitude of one isolated window-shaped peak, but neither creates the independent evidence needed to separate components already merged by a finite observation.
single_conceptual_move.success_test: After the lesson, the reader can choose between a denser FFT/interpolator and a longer acquisition, state the assumptions behind the choice, and reject a two-bump display whose peak locations move with relative phase.
keeper_facts: With N acquired samples and transform length L at sample rate f_s, the evaluation spacing is f_s/L, while observation time remains N/f_s.

For three neighboring dB magnitudes alpha, beta, gamma, p=(1/2)(alpha-gamma)/(alpha-2beta+gamma) and the fitted peak is beta-(1/4)(alpha-gamma)p; both estimates inherit the single-windowed-peak model.
Two visible maxima are not resolution unless their locations and separation survive the declared relative-phase perturbation.

throughline: Ref the window lesson with a reminder that N acquired, windowed samples already fix the continuous main-lobe shape; Ref the FFT lesson with a reminder that L controls where that curve is evaluated.
State the move as a decision boundary between single-peak localization and multi-component resolution.
retrieval_task: State the difference between N acquired samples and an L-point FFT with L at least N.
For fixed f_s, name which quantity changes observation time and which changes only frequency-grid spacing.
Recall which two window measurements govern close equal tones and a weak tone beside a strong one.
State the course forward-transform sign and amplitude-calibration convention needed before comparing peak heights.
opening_and_retrieval.placement: One Task with folded answers immediately after the throughline; no prerequisite derivation in the body.

argument_sections.heading: A denser grid samples the same finite-record spectrum
argument_sections.claim: Holding the first N samples and w[n] fixed while increasing L changes omega_k=2*pi*k/L and f_k=k*f_s/L, but not the finite-record DTFT, observation time N/f_s, or main-lobe width in physical frequency.
argument_sections.concrete_entry: Use one periodic-Hann-windowed analytic tone with N=64 at original-bin coordinate 10.3. Compare L=64 and L=1024, then acquire N=256 samples at the same normalized tone frequency and window convention.
argument_sections.formal_apparatus: Give the exact spectral-resolution definition from concepts.yaml after the comparison; use N only for acquired/window length and L only for FFT evaluation length.
argument_sections.reversal: The L=1024 curve looks smoother and its largest sample lies closer to the peak, but only the N=256 curve becomes physically narrower.
argument_sections.bearing: This fixes what padding can legitimately improve before an estimator is introduced.

argument_sections.heading: Three local samples estimate one isolated peak
argument_sections.claim: A parabola fitted to three neighboring log-magnitude samples supplies a fractional-bin frequency and peak-height estimate only when those samples describe one concave local maximum.
argument_sections.concrete_entry: Work a non-exercise example with declared alpha, beta, gamma, k-star, L, f_s, periodic window, raw-forward scale, and complex-versus-real amplitude convention; compute p, fitted dB height, frequency, and coherent-gain-corrected amplitude without skipping algebra.
argument_sections.formal_apparatus: Derive neither formula here; state p and fitted height, require alpha-2beta+gamma not equal to zero and |p| at most 1/2 under a correctly selected center bin, and pair the example immediately with Exercise 1.
argument_sections.reversal: A peak-height correction is not a universal amplitude correction: coherent response, one-sided real-signal scaling, and the accuracy of the parabolic model remain separate clauses.
argument_sections.bearing: The method improves localization while exposing the assumptions that limit the estimate.

argument_sections.heading: Padding reduces sampling error until model error dominates
argument_sections.claim: Parabolic interpolation is exact at a sampled peak and at the half-bin symmetry case, but is generally biased between them because practical window transforms are not exact parabolas on a dB scale.
argument_sections.concrete_entry: Sweep an isolated analytic tone across one original bin under declared periodic windows and padding factors 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32; report worst absolute frequency error in original-bin units and peak-amplitude error in dB.
argument_sections.formal_apparatus: Define bias here as systematic estimator error from model mismatch, not random scatter. If the plotted curves include a nonzero asymptote, introduce a frozen neighboring tone or noise floor and label that floor as model contamination; do not draw a false irreducible floor for the noiseless isolated-tone case, whose error tends toward zero with dense sampling.
argument_sections.reversal: Zero padding introduces no new bias by itself, yet it also cannot remove bias caused by a violated single-peak model.
argument_sections.bearing: The estimator's numerical refinement is now separated from the validity of its signal model.

argument_sections.heading: Relative phase can manufacture two misleading maxima
argument_sections.claim: Under-resolved sinusoids add coherently, so changing only their relative phase can create, erase, or move apparent maxima before the observation supports stable component estimates.
argument_sections.concrete_entry: Recreate the source's rectangular-window equal-tone experiment at fixed separation with in-phase and 90-degree-quadrature cases, plot true-frequency guides, and annotate the displacement of measured maxima.
argument_sections.formal_apparatus: Define the lesson's operational resolution check as two maxima whose locations remain within a declared tolerance under the tested relative phases; do not elevate this one check into a universal theorem.
argument_sections.reversal: Two bumps can be less trustworthy than one: the quadrature display can appear resolved while both reported frequencies are biased.
argument_sections.bearing: The visual criterion becomes a stability test rather than a count of bumps.

argument_sections.heading: Choose acquisition for resolution and interpolation for localization
argument_sections.claim: The correct action follows from the claim being made: densify and interpolate for one isolated peak on a fixed record; acquire a longer informative record or change the window/model for component separation.
argument_sections.concrete_entry: Close with a two-row decision ledger: fixed N=64 isolated off-bin tone versus two tones inside the N=64 window main lobe, with grid spacing, duration, main-lobe width, estimator assumptions, and failure checks in separate columns.
argument_sections.formal_apparatus: No new theorem. End by naming what is established and by stating that the next lesson treats random squared-magnitude spectra as estimators rather than deterministic tone coordinates.
argument_sections.reversal: The larger FFT is sometimes the efficient correct tool, but only for the localization claim it can support.
argument_sections.bearing: The lesson's single move is converted into an auditable engineering choice.

sequence.name: PaddingVersusObservation
sequence.placement: section 1 after the N=64, L=64 concrete spectrum
frame_contract: Frame 1: N=64 acquired periodic-Hann samples, L=64; continuous normalized magnitude curve plus coarse sample dots; duration 64/f_s and grid f_s/64 labeled.
Frame 2: keep every sample, window, axis, and continuous curve pixel-identical; change only L to 1024 and add the 16-times denser sample dots; main-lobe width label stays fixed.
Frame 3: change acquired length to N=256 at the same f_s and normalized tone frequency, keep L=1024, and show the genuinely narrower curve; duration and main-lobe labels update.
sequence.task: Before frame 3, predict which labels can change when only L changes; then identify the first frame in which resolving evidence changes.
sequence.alt: Three fixed-axis frames show the same 64-sample windowed-tone spectrum sampled on 64 and 1024 point grids, followed by a 256-sample observation whose main lobe is physically narrower.

single_figures.name: PeakParabolaFit
single_figures.content: Three colored dB samples alpha, beta, gamma at k-star minus one, k-star, k-star plus one; a fitted concave parabola; vertex offset p; KaTeX formulas for p and fitted height; a bottom mapping from k-star+p to (k-star+p)f_s/L.
single_figures.reason_for_tier: The figure binds prose labels, symbols, and two formulas; real KaTeX and responsive HTML are required.
single_figures.alt: Three adjacent log-magnitude samples define a concave fitted parabola whose vertex lies p bins from the largest sample and supplies the interpolated peak height.

single_figures.name: InterpolationErrorByPadding
single_figures.content: Log-x padding factor versus worst absolute frequency error in original-bin units for the declared periodic windows; a companion amplitude-error strip may share the x-axis. Every curve is generated from course formulas, not traced. Any nonzero floor must be labeled with its frozen contamination source; isolated noiseless curves must be permitted to approach zero.
single_figures.reason_for_tier: This is a compact numeric plot with short labels and no long prose or displayed math.
single_figures.alt: Peak-interpolation error falls as the same spectrum is sampled more densely, with window-dependent rates and any contamination floor explicitly separated from grid error.

single_figures.name: PhaseFalseResolution
single_figures.placement: section 4 immediately after the in-phase/quadrature comparison
single_figures.content: Two fixed-axis near-identical panels for equal tones: in phase and 90 degrees apart. True frequencies use thin guides; measured local maxima use colored markers and numeric offsets; a bottom verdict distinguishes stable component locations from phase-created bumps.
single_figures.reason_for_tier: Aligned panels, sentence-length verdicts, numeric offset labels, and semantic binding exceed a robust raw-SVG label budget.
single_figures.alt: Two equal-tone spectra with identical frequencies and record length but different relative phase show that apparent peak count and peak location can change while the physical tones do not.

single_figures.name: LocalizationResolutionLedger
single_figures.content: Two aligned rows map claim, evidence held fixed, permissible action, changed quantity, and failure check: isolated-tone localization maps to larger L plus interpolation; two-tone separation maps to longer N or a changed window/model.
single_figures.reason_for_tier: This is the lesson's signature decision figure and key-image candidate; flowing text must stack cleanly on mobile.
single_figures.alt: A decision ledger sends a fixed-record isolated peak to denser sampling and interpolation, but sends unresolved components to longer acquisition or a changed model.

visual_plan.density_rule: Place a visual, Task, environment, or heading at least every three prose paragraphs; do not add decorative FFT grids or repeat the predecessor's window-family comparison.

interactive_demo.justification: course.yaml deliberately sets demo: null. A new slider that changes N, L, phase, or tone separation would duplicate PaddingVsDataLab and WeakToneWindowLab and would not add a new learner action beyond the prediction-driven sequence and phase comparison. The static apparatus can hold axes and conditions fixed, which is essential to the conceptual distinction.
interactive_demo.interactive_role_replaced_by: The FigureSequence carries a prediction-before-reveal Task, and the phase figure carries a falsification Task: accept two-tone resolution only if both maxima stay within the declared tolerance under all displayed phases.
interactive_demo.reconsider_only_if: A later audit finds that readers cannot discriminate N from L after the fixed-frame sequence; any future demo must test a target, remain under the existing course entry only after human syllabus approval, and must not be a free curve-moving sandbox.

exercise_plan.placement: Exercise 1 is the in-body worked-example pair in section 2; Exercises 2 through 6 form the closing Exercises section.

exercises.prompt: With alpha=-12 dB, beta=0 dB, gamma=-6 dB at bins 19, 20, 21 and grid spacing 10 Hz, compute p, the interpolated frequency, and the fitted peak height; state the zero-denominator boundary and isolated-peak assumption.
exercises.full_solution_obligations: Show p=(1/2)(-12+6)/(-12-0-6)=1/6, f_hat=(20+1/6)10=201.67 Hz, and fitted height 0-(1/4)(-12+6)(1/6)=0.25 dB. State that a zero denominator gives zero fitted curvature and no unique finite vertex, and that three samples must belong to one concave isolated peak. Do not turn 0.25 dB into physical amplitude without a stated DFT/window/real-signal scale.

exercises.prompt: Diagnose an exactly bin-centered tone, an exactly half-bin tone, zero amplitude, and two coincident tones under the declared estimator.
exercises.full_solution_obligations: For each case state identifiability, expected p or tie behavior, and amplitude conditions. Bin-centered gives p=0; half-bin gives symmetric tied centers and equivalent p=+/-1/2 if indexing is consistent; zero amplitude makes log magnitude and frequency undefined; coincident tones reduce to one phasor sum and cannot reveal two frequencies, with opposite phases able to cancel to the zero-amplitude case.

exercises.prompt: Refute 'two visible bumps imply unbiased frequency estimates' using the fixed in-phase and phase-quadrature equal-tone experiment.
exercises.full_solution_obligations: Identify the false inference from local-maxima count to component identification, compare every measured maximum against the true-frequency guides, show that changing only relative phase moves or creates the maxima, and state the replacement criterion: two estimates must remain stable under the declared phase perturbations. The conclusion must be scoped to the frozen window, separation, and record length.

exercises.prompt: Starting from y(x)=a(x-p)^2+b at x=-1,0,1, derive p and b from alpha, beta, gamma and diagnose the zero-denominator case.
exercises.full_solution_obligations: Write all three equations, subtract them to obtain alpha-gamma=4ap, derive a=(alpha-2beta+gamma)/2, substitute to obtain p and b=beta-(alpha-gamma)p/4, then explain that zero curvature makes p undefined and positive curvature describes a minimum rather than a spectral peak.

exercises.prompt: Choose and defend a plan for (a) locating one isolated off-bin tone from a fixed 64-sample record and (b) separating two tones inside that record's window main lobe. Report grid spacing, observation duration, and main-lobe width in original-bin units.
exercises.full_solution_obligations: For (a), hold N and w fixed, increase L, interpolate, and retain the single-peak/model checks. For (b), acquire a longer informative record or change the declared window/model; increasing L alone is rejected. Explicitly retrieve the predecessor's main-lobe and coherent-calibration concepts and the FFT lesson's length/scale contract, and keep physical tone frequencies fixed while N changes.

exercises.prompt: Generate 50 seeded, equal-length white-noise records, hold N, window, FFT length, scale, and one interior bin fixed, and report the 50 squared magnitudes, their mean, sample standard deviation, and coefficient of variation. Explain why one smooth zero-padded trace cannot remove the observed trial-to-trial spread.
exercises.full_solution_obligations: Supply executable NumPy or equivalent pseudocode with the seed and every normalization, compute rather than merely describe the summary statistics, distinguish the fixed deterministic DTFT grid from variation across realizations, and state that averaging or a probabilistic estimator is now required. End with exactly this sole forward link: <Ref lesson="correlation-psd-and-welch">Correlation, PSD, and Welch Estimation</Ref>. Do not define PSD or claim Welch's variance law here.

exercise_plan.global_solution_standard: Every solution shows setup, arithmetic or inference, boundary conditions, units, and the transferable decision; no 'left to the reader', unstated software output, or answer-only verdict is permitted.
exercise_plan.constraint_audit: Exactly one item is marked warm_up=true (Exercise 1). Exactly one exercise is forward-reaching (Exercise 6), and its solution contains the only forward Ref to correlation-psd-and-welch.

novice_jargon_ledger.binding: The N acquired samples span N/f_s under the course half-open record convention; use 'record duration' first and introduce 'aperture' only as the parenthetical standard term.
novice_jargon_ledger.confusion_to_prevent: Do not call the L-N appended zeros additional observation time.

novice_jargon_ledger.binding: Number of frequency coordinates evaluated after the N acquired/windowed samples are followed by zeros; f_k=k f_s/L.
novice_jargon_ledger.confusion_to_prevent: Never reuse N for both acquisition length and padded transform length.

novice_jargon_ledger.binding: Use the concepts.yaml definition verbatim: ability of a finite observation and window to support distinct frequency claims, not plotted FFT-sample spacing.
novice_jargon_ledger.confusion_to_prevent: Avoid the phrase 'FFT resolution' unless immediately split into grid spacing versus physical resolving power.

novice_jargon_ledger.binding: One original bin means f_s/N for the acquired record; a padded-grid step is N/L original bins.
novice_jargon_ledger.confusion_to_prevent: A padded bin and an original bin are different units.

novice_jargon_ledger.binding: A local parabola fitted to the three log-magnitude samples around one selected maximum; use 'parabolic' as the primary name and note 'quadratic' once.
novice_jargon_ledger.confusion_to_prevent: It interpolates a model of the peak, not the time samples and not arbitrary neighboring components.

novice_jargon_ledger.binding: Signed displacement from the largest sampled bin k-star, normally in [-1/2,1/2] after correct center selection.
novice_jargon_ledger.confusion_to_prevent: p is dimensionless; multiply by f_s/L for hertz.

novice_jargon_ledger.binding: Systematic difference between the estimator and the true tone parameter caused here by peak-model mismatch; random scatter is not called bias.
novice_jargon_ledger.confusion_to_prevent: Zero padding itself is ideal spectral sampling and does not create interpolation bias.

novice_jargon_ledger.binding: Re-anchor to complex-sinusoids-and-phasors: overlapping complex contributions add as phasors, so magnitude depends on their angle difference.
novice_jargon_ledger.confusion_to_prevent: Phase does not change the physical tone frequencies, but it can move maxima of their finite-record sum.

novice_jargon_ledger.first_use: not introduced in body; optional only in Exercise 6 solution handoff
novice_jargon_ledger.binding: Call the computed object 'one record's squared-magnitude spectrum' here; the next lesson owns the formal estimator name and normalization.
novice_jargon_ledger.confusion_to_prevent: Do not treat one random record as a deterministic tone spectrum or a converged PSD.

global: All visuals require one-sentence factual alt text that states the comparison or displacement; captions state the inference, not visual navigation.
Color never carries a distinction alone: use solid/dashed lines, point shapes, direct labels, and panel headers; preserve at least 3:1 non-text and 4.5:1 text contrast in both themes.
Use the house amber for the estimated/current peak and blue for truth/reference, with the role named on the figure wherever first introduced.
Minimum plotted label size is 12 px at the shipped view; no rotated labels, hover-only values, or text embedded below legibility.
Every equation in a component figure uses KaTeX through M; raw SVGs contain only short labels and curves.
sequence: All three frames use one identical viewBox, axes, dB range, curve placement, and annotation anchors; only the declared delta changes.
Previous/next controls must be keyboard and touch usable with a visible focus state and at least 44 by 44 CSS-pixel targets.
The caption and nearby Task must remain meaningful if motion or stepping is unavailable; frame numbers name N and L in text.
component_figures: PeakParabolaFit stacks the formula below the plot below 560 px and never relies on three side-by-side formula cards.
PhaseFalseResolution stacks its panels vertically on a phone while preserving identical axes; true-frequency guides remain labeled in both panels.
LocalizationResolutionLedger becomes two vertical cards below 640 px, each repeating its row headers so horizontal scrolling is unnecessary.
plot: InterpolationErrorByPadding directly labels curve endpoints or uses a short shape-coded legend below the plot; do not place a dense legend over data.
A log axis is explicitly labeled 'padding factor L/N' with visible ticks 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32; the y-axis includes units in original bins or dB.

redundancy_traps: Do not re-derive finite-window spectral convolution or repeat the predecessor's window metric table; one Ref plus a reminder clause is sufficient.
Do not repeat the DFT lesson's PaddingVsDataLab narrative or imply that this lesson newly discovers zero padding as DTFT sampling; use that fact to delimit the estimator.
Do not re-teach FFT algorithms, cost, bit reversal, or library conventions; only retrieve L, sign, scale, and output order when they affect the estimate.

Do not let PaddingVersusObservation, InterpolationErrorByPadding, and LocalizationResolutionLedger all state 'padding is not resolution' in the same way: the sequence shows the invariant curve, the plot measures estimator error, and the ledger makes the engineering choice.
Do not make PeakParabolaFit's caption restate its formulas; the caption states the single-peak assumption and the prose performs the calculation.
Do not present a nonzero asymptotic error floor for a noiseless isolated peak without a declared contaminant; that would contradict ideal spectral interpolation.
Do not use 'two peaks' as the definition of spectral resolution; the phase figure must show why stability and location accuracy are additional conditions.
Do not define random process, PSD, autocorrelation, periodogram consistency, or Welch averaging; Exercise 6 creates the need and hands off once.
Do not add a demo merely to expose N, L, phase, and separation sliders; existing course demos already cover those manipulations and would make this lesson redundant.
implementation_holds: Before drawing numeric curves, freeze window endpoint convention, analytic-versus-real signal, N, L set, tone coordinates, phase set, dB floor, amplitude normalization, peak-selection rule, and resolution tolerance in the figure-generation handoff.
Render-and-look every figure in light, dark, and narrow mobile widths. The figure plan is approved; the plotted numerical outcomes still require generated-data verification before publication.
